sections.name: DEFAULT_PROFILE
sections.title: Fallback look for unknown materials
sections.what: A grey-blue, fairly matte look used when a material name is not in the table, so unrecognised parts still show up.
sections.why: Likely reason: an unknown part should stay visible rather than vanish.
sections.watch_out: The fallback is silent, so a missing key looks like an ordinary part and gives no error.

sections.name: materialProfile
sections.title: Look up a material by name
sections.what: Returns the table entry for a given name, or the fallback when the name is missing or not in the table.
sections.why: A single safe lookup means callers never receive an empty value.
sections.watch_out: The match is exact. A near-miss name silently receives the fallback look.

summary: Holds the named surface looks (colour, shine and metal feel) that the 3D view uses for each kind of facility surface, and supplies a neutral look for unknown names.
purpose: Give each named surface a consistent appearance, so a concrete pad, steel frame or water pond looks right, and let anyone tune appearance in one place.
why: Likely reason: keeping appearance in one table means every model uses the same look for the same surface. The rationale notes say the values are generic, not taken from a specific supplier.
how: First, a profile shape is defined with four values. Second, a table of about forty named surfaces is filled with colour, roughness and metalness values, each with a short rationale. Third, a default profile is defined for unknown names. Finally, a lookup returns the matching table entry, or the default when the name is missing or empty.
inputs: A text key naming the surface, such as the material name stored on a model part. The key may be missing.
outputs: A profile with colour, roughness, metalness and rationale. Always a valid profile, never empty.
risks: The values are visual estimates, not measured data. A misspelled key silently gets the grey-blue default, which looks like a plain part rather than an error. Spelling is mixed: chain-link uses the British spelling galvanised while other entries use galvanized.
debug: If a part has the wrong colour or shine, find its key name and check the matching entry here. If it looks plain grey-blue, the key probably does not match an entry. Compare the spelling with the table exactly. Run materials.test.ts after any change.
